    🌙 Spasian Faith¶

    "The Prophet saw the Silver Light. We carry it forward."

    The Spasian Faith is the state religion of the Spasian Teocracy in East Erisdar, founded around the teachings of the Prophet Spasius during the chaos of the Lost Era (399–300 BGD). Unlike the Erisian Church, which venerates Eris as a divine figure, the Spasian faith holds that divinity resides in The Silver Bride — the planetary ring that encircles Ge'or. The ring's light is a direct conduit to the creator.

    Origins¶

    Spasius emerged during the worst century of Ge'orian history. The destruction of Baoth had thrown the continent into anarchy. Warlords ruled. Famine killed forty percent of the population. The Erisian cult was still consolidating, not yet dominant.

    In this darkness, Spasius claimed to receive visions from the Silver Bride — the thin luminous band stretching horizon to horizon. He preached that the ring was not a celestial accident but a message: a line of divine light connecting every corner of the world, visible to all, belonging to none. His followers, the Argentines (from the ancient word for silver), spread across eastern Erisdar, establishing a faith that answered the despair of the age with the promise that the divine was visible — not hidden in temples or controlled by priests, but painted across the sky for anyone with eyes to see.

    Beliefs¶

    • The Silver Bride is divine — the ring is not a natural phenomenon. It is the creator's signature, left visible so that no one can claim the divine is absent.
    • The Argent Codex — the collected writings of Spasius, interpreted by the Council of Illuminants. It contains prophecies, moral teachings, and astrological calculations.
    • The Ring-Cycle — the ring's phases govern the liturgical calendar. Major civic decisions are deferred to astrologically favorable conjunctions. A decision made under the wrong phase invites failure.
    • No intermediaries — the Spasian faith rejects the Erisian model of a church hierarchy mediating between the faithful and the divine. Anyone can look up.

    Practices¶

    • Ring-watching — the central devotional act. The faithful gather at dawn and dusk to observe the Silver Bride and recite passages from the Argent Codex.
    • Astrological governance — the Council of Illuminants, a body of twenty-one high priests, interprets the ring's phases. They select their own members from the priestly caste.
    • Missionary work — Spasian missionaries travel to neighboring lands. The Fractured State of Erislod regularly sends them back.

    Relations with Other Faiths¶

    • Erisian Church — the Pontificate considers Spasian doctrine heretical. The Spasian clergy consider the Erisians spiritually blind — worshiping a fabricated goddess when the real divine is visible in the sky.
    • Silver Republic — the neighboring nation shares a coast and a name with Spasia but little else. The Republic views Spasian mysticism as anachronistic; Spasia views Republican secularism as a spiritual vacancy. Relations are tense but non-belligerent.

    Influence¶

    • State religion of the Spasian Teocracy (capital: Spasia) in East Erisdar.
    • Minority presence in the Silver Republic and Fractured State of Erislod.

    Connections¶
